facts.q: What is a life cycle?
facts.a: the stages a living thing goes through
d: the places a living thing visits
the food a living thing likes best
the sounds a living thing makes
facts.explain: A life cycle is every stage from the start of a life to the making of the next one.

facts.q: Does a life cycle ever start again?
facts.explain: Each grown-up produces young, and their cycle starts over — that is why it is a cycle.

facts.q: What comes out of an egg?
facts.explain: An egg holds a young animal while it grows enough to come out.

facts.q: What is the change from caterpillar to butterfly called?
facts.explain: Metamorphosis means a complete change of body, not just growing bigger.

facts.q: What must a seed have to start growing?
facts.explain: Water and warmth wake a seed up; without them it just waits.

bio.1.lifecycles.pair_explain: Young organisms change as they grow. Some look like small adults; others change body form dramatically.
bio.1.lifecycles.sequence_explain: Begin at the stage named and follow development. A cycle repeats, so its starting point must be stated.

math.1.place-value.sequence_prompt: Put them in order, smallest first
math.1.place-value.sequence_say: Tap the numbers in order, from the smallest to the biggest.

facts.q: In twenty-three, how many tens are there?
facts.explain: Twenty is two tens.

facts.q: In twenty-three, how many ones are left over?
facts.explain: Twenty-three is two tens and three ones left over.

facts.q: What do ten ones make?
facts.explain: Ten ones bundle up into one ten.

facts.q: What do ten tens make?
facts.explain: Ten tens bundle up into one hundred.

facts.q: Which is bigger, forty or fourteen?
d: forty and fourteen are the same
facts.explain: Forty is four tens; fourteen is one ten and four.

facts.q: Which digit in a two-digit number counts the tens?
facts.explain: In a two-digit number the left digit counts tens, the right counts ones.

math.1.place-value.pair_explain: Ten ones make one ten. The place of a digit tells you how many groups of that size it represents.
math.1.place-value.sequence_explain: Compare the highest place first. If those digits match, move to the next place.

facts.q: What number comes after nineteen?
facts.explain: Nineteen, twenty — twenty is the next one.

facts.q: Which number is bigger, eleven or seven?
facts.explain: Eleven is further along when you count up.

facts.q: How many fingers are on two hands?
facts.explain: Five on one hand and five on the other.

facts.q: If you count on two from twelve, where do you land?
facts.explain: Twelve, thirteen, fourteen — two steps on.

facts.q: Which number is the smallest?
facts.explain: Three comes first when you count up from one.

facts.q: Counting backwards from twenty, what comes first?
facts.explain: Counting back, the number before twenty is nineteen.

math.0.numbers20.pair_explain: Counting on adds one. Say the next number in the counting sequence, even when crossing from nine to ten.
math.0.numbers20.sequence_explain: Count forward one step at a time. Compare the numbers' values rather than how long their names look.
